title: Removal of CCR5 ligands and induction of pro-resolving lipid mediators by apoptotic neutrophils during resolution
protocol: Procure WT and Ccr5 minus/minus mice from animal facility.
Label mice on tail and weigh them.
Prepare chart to record animal number, weight, treatment, time of zymosan A injection, time of sacrifice, and volume of lavage fluid collected.
Anesthetize mice with isoflurane in prepared chamber.
Alternatively anesthetize mice by placing their head in a tube containing wet kimwipes.
Inject 1 ml of zymosan A i.p. to each mouse.
Return the animals to their container for 4 hr.
Sacrifice animals using a lethal dose of isoflurane.
Test reflexes by gently pinching hands and feet with tweezers.
Place the mouse face-up on a Styrofoam surface.
Secure the mouse by pinning down its hands and feet with needles.
Incise a small bit of skin over the anterior abdominal wall using forceps and scissors.
Inject 5 ml DPBS minus/minus i.p. to the exposed peritoneum.
Massage shake the abdomen to disperse cells in the lavage fluid.
Cut away a skin flap and raise and extend it superiorly, inferiorly, and laterally.
Collect as much of the lavage fluid as possible with a 5 ml syringe from both sides of the lateral abdomen if needed.
Tilt the mouse’s side downward for better collection aided by gravity.
Note the volume and clarity of the solution.
Place the collected fluid in 15 ml plastic tubes.
Keep the samples on ice.
Rinse Hemocytometer and cover slip in ethanol and water.
Prepare a small Eppendorf tube per sample with the appropriate dilution of trypan blue stain and sample for 2hr, 4hr, 12hr, 24hr, or 28hr time points.
Lightly mix cells and add to trypan blue stain in tube, then gently mix up and down with pipette tip.
Load 10 μl of solution onto each side of hemocytometer.
Count the 4 corner squares of the hemocytometer under light microscope at 10x magnification or 40x if necessary.
Repeat for other side of hemocytometer.
Rinse hemocytometer with ethanol and water before moving to the next sample.
Prepare one slide for each mouse.
Mix cell samples again.
Add 100 μl sample + 300 μl 15% BSA.
Place slides in cytospin, screw on the lid, and spin at 1600 rpm for 4 minutes.
Extract excess fluid and carefully remove slides.
Let dry overnight.
Stain slides by placing them sequentially in Wright-Giemsa stain for 30 seconds.
Place stained slides in sodium phosphate buffer (50 mM, pH 7.2) for 2 minutes.
Rinse slides in de-ionized water for 10 seconds.
Let the slides dry for at least 2 hours.
Count 100 total cells using a light microscope and assign them to cell categories.
Repeat counting in a different area 1-2 times for a total of 200-300 cells per slide.
Spin down cells from exudates at 1300 RPM for 5 minutes.
Aspirate the liquid above the cell pellet.
Resuspend the pellet in 300 μl of FACS buffer containing FITC-conjugated anti-Ly-6G antibodies (1:100) and PE-conjugated anti-F4/80 antibodies (1:200).
Incubate the cells for 20 minutes over ice.
Wash the cells with 500 μl of FACS buffer.
Spin down the cells again.
Resuspend the pellet in 5 ml of FACS buffer and transfer to FACS tubes.
Prepare the settings of the FACS machine for flow-sorting.
Place the tube in the FACS machine and start the sorting.
Analyze the acquired cells to determine PMN purity.
Count the cells and calculate the total number of cells.
Spin down the cells and resuspend them in culture medium at a concentration of 1x10^6/ml.
Incubate overnight at incubator in culture plates to promote apoptosis of PMN.
Collect PMN from culture plates, count them, and spin down the cells.
Resuspend the cells (2.5x10^6/mouse in 1 ml of saline) and inject them i.p. to recipient mice.
Spin down the cells after injection.
Take a sample for cell counting and verify the quality of the exudate recovery (no bleeding).
Collect the supernatants.
Freeze supernatants and store at -20°C.
Prepare the working wash solution as a 1:20 dilution in deionized water.
Reconstitute standard in 1 ml of a standard diluent (50% assay diluent and 50% PBS) for luminex analysis.
Let the reconstituted standard sit for at least 10 minutes.
Add 300 μl of standard diluent to each of 7 Eppendorf tubes.
Perform a 1:3 serial dilution from Standard 1 to create Standards 2-7, leaving Standard 8 as a blank.
Thaw samples.
Vortex antibody conjugated beads for 30 seconds.
Sonicate antibody conjugated beads for 30 seconds.
Dispense antibody conjugated beads to re-suspend them.
Mix 250 μl of each analyte bead solution with 1.25 ml wash solution in an aluminum foil-wrapped test tube.
Pre-wet a 96-well filter-bottomed plate by pipetting 0.2 ml wash solution into each well.
Assemble vacuum manifold and calibrate the pressure to -5 in Hg.
Let wash solution soak in wells for 15 to 30 seconds, then aspirate liquid with vacuum manifold.
Blot bottom of filter plate on clean paper towel then with kimwipes to rid of any excess liquid.
Vortex bead solution briefly.
Pipette 25 μl of the bead solution into each well.
Keep plate and beads shielded from light using an aluminum foil-wrapped plate cover.
Repeat wash step twice as stated in Step 36.
Pipette 50 μl of incubation buffer into each well.
Pipette 50 μl assay diluent into rows 3 – 12 to prepare for the samples.
Add 50 μl of sample into designated wells.
Pipette 100 μl of standards into designated wells in rows 1 – 2 to create the standard curve.
Cover plate and incubate for 2 hours at room temperature on an orbital shaker set to 300 rpm to keep beads suspended.
Repeat wash step as stated in Step 36 twice.
During the 2-hour incubation, mix 1 ml of each analyte biotinylated secondary antibody with 5 ml biotin diluent for a 5-analyte multiplex assay preparation.
Pipette 100 μl of diluted biotinylated detector antibody into each well.
Cover plate and incubate for 1 hour at room temperature on an orbital shaker set to 300 rpm.
Ten minutes before the end of the 1-hour incubation, dilute 1.0 ml Streptavidin – RPE concentrate in an aluminum foil-wrapped test tube with 9.0 ml Streptavidin Diluent.
Repeat wash step as stated in Step 36 twice.
Pipette 100 μl of diluted Streptavidin – RPE solution into each well.
Cover plate and incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature on an orbital shaker set to 300 rpm.
Turn on the Luminex 100 instrument.
Open the Luminex 100 data collection software.
Prime the system three times.
Eject the XY platform.
Fill the reservoir half full with ethanol.
Retract the platform.
Wash the reservoir two times with water.
Indicate the instrument to warm up.
Calibrate the instrument with calibration beads.
Select wells for both classification beads and reporter beads in the Setup XY menu.
Enter the Lot # for each set of calibration beads.
Put 5 drops of each bead solution into its designated well.
Insert the plate into the XY platform and click Start to calibrate.
Wash the reservoir six times with deionized water.
Begin a new session in the software.
Adjust settings: Events: 100, Bead Region Count: 96, Sample Size: 50 μl, Gate Low: 7800, Gate High: 15200.
Set up template in software and enter bead regions from Information Sheets into Bead Set menu.
Enter standard concentrations.
Repeat wash step as stated in Step 34 three times.
Pipette 100 μl of wash solution into wells.
Set the wells on an orbital shaker for at least one minute prior to analysis.
Insert uncovered plate into the XY Platform of the Luminex 100.
Click "Apply" and "OK" in the software to begin analysis.
Create a standard curve in the data analysis software.
Determine the concentration of samples from this curve.
Multiply the values by 2 to correct for the 1:2 dilution.
